title: HYTE: Flexible Tiling for Sparse Accelerators via Hybrid Static-Dynamic Approaches
problem: Tiling very large sparse tensors on specialized hardware accelerators is challenged by the inability of purely static schemes (which use simple heuristics without adapting to local sparsity patterns) and purely dynamic schemes (which have high design complexity) to jointly find near-optimal tile size/shape, dimension iteration order, buffer allocation, and metadata management while accommodating highly varying local data sparsity.
motivation: Sparse tensor operations dominate many ML and scientific workloads; as tensor sizes exceed on-chip buffer capacity, tiling becomes mandatory, but the high variability of sparsity distributions within a tensor makes a single static tiling scheme leave significant performance on the table, while fully dynamic schemes add unacceptable hardware complexity.
method: HYTE is a hybrid static-dynamic tiling framework for sparse accelerators. An offline static scheduler first samples the sparse matrix to estimate a near-optimal initial tiling configuration — covering tile size and shape, dimension iteration order across tiles, and buffer allocation policies — without analyzing the full tensor. At runtime, a dynamic tuning mechanism adjusts tile shape on-the-fly to maintain high buffer utilization as local sparsity patterns vary. HYTE also manages tiling metadata in both off-chip memory and on-chip buffer efficiently, handling the non-negligible metadata overhead that prior sparse tiling schemes neglect.
key_novelty: HYTE's combination of a lightweight offline sampling-based static scheduler with a runtime tile-shape dynamic tuner is the first to jointly optimize all tiling dimensions (size, shape, iteration order, allocation) while actively adapting to local sparsity variation.
contributions: A static offline scheduler that uses lightweight sampling to identify near-optimal initial tiling configurations across tile size/shape, iteration order, and buffer allocation without full tensor analysis.
A dynamic runtime mechanism for tile shape adjustment that maintains high buffer utilization under highly variable local sparsity patterns.
Efficient on-chip and off-chip metadata management for tiling on sparse accelerators.
3.3x to 6.2x geomean speedup over state-of-the-art sparse tiling strategies across diverse sparse matrices.

metrics.speedup: 3.3x to 6.2x geomean over state-of-the-art sparse tiling strategies

baselines: state-of-the-art sparse tiling strategies (static and dynamic, unspecified)
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation is limited to sparse matrices and may not generalize to sparse tensors with higher-order structure.
primary_theme: Hybrid static-dynamic tiling for sparse tensor accelerators
